newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rubber prices mixed in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rubber prices mixed in late trade.

text.p: Indonesian tyre-grade SIR20 offer prices ended mixed in late dull trading on Tuesday and sentiment remained weak due to a lack of buyers, traders said.
"Prices have improved a bit after deals were done today in Palembang and Medan. But in general, sentiment remains weak because not many buyers coming to the market," said one trader.
Traders said deals were quoted at 53.50 U.S. cents/lb in Medan while in Palembang, offer prices rose to 53.625, up from 53.25-53.50 in the morning.
They said Surabaya followed the rise in Medan and levels were quoted there at 53.50, up 0.25 cents from the morning.
In Padang, SIR20 was firmer at 53.25, up from 53.00 in the morning, but levels were unchanged at 53.00 in Pontianak and Jambi, traders said.
Some traders said offers were still heard at 54.00 U.S. cents/lb fob Medan and Padang because supply was a little bit tight.
"We heard some traders offer SIR20 at 54.00, but I think it's not going to work because buyers are still reluctant to buy even if we offer rubber at 53.00 U.S. cents/lb," said one trader.
Traders said some dealers still took a wait-and-see stance to see an improvement in offer prices.
"But I don't know if they can stand not to sell for a long period when prices continue to decline. They have to sell because they need cash," said another trader.
Traders said the sluggish demand might be caused by the fact that many buyers already had enough stock. Some said buyers turned to Cambodia, Thailand and Vietnam for cheaper prices.
Some traders said they believed tight supply and the current wintering would force offer prices to decline further.
